ui.source.p0.v.p1.de.nieuw.project.wizar:
{p0} v{p1}

    The New Project Wizard creates a new project folder with a clean base structure.

    Supported starters:
    - Python CLI
    - PowerShell tool
    - Rust CLI
    - .NET console
    - Node.js
    - Expo / React Native base
    - Raspberry Pi Python
    - Arduino .ino
    - PlatformIO ESP32
    - PlatformIO ESP8266
    - Empty project

    The wizard can create automatically:
    - README.md
    - .gitignore
    - CHANGELOG.md
    - TODO.md
    - .projectmanager.json
    - starter files per project type

    Important:
    - No dependencies are installed.
    - Nothing is built automatically.
    - Git init is optional and works only when Git is found.
    - An existing non-empty folder is not populated without confirmation.
ui.source.p0.v.p1.project.intelligence.i:
{p0} v{p1}

    Project Intelligence is a local analysis layer.

    Signals used:
    - project type and structure
    - documentation such as README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG and TODO
    - build readiness and latest build status
    - workflow status
    - project family and duplicate signals
    - age since last change
    - cleanup candidates and risks

    The score consists of:
    - Structure
    - Documentation
    - Buildability
    - Maintainability
    - Risk
    - Duplicate likelihood

    Important:
    - No external AI/API is used.
    - Deletion never happens automatically.
    - Apply recommendation performs only safe actions such as changing workflow status or creating document templates.
    - v4.2 can also apply safe recommendations to a selection through Intelligence Action Center.
    - Deletion, cleanup and builds are never run automatically by Intelligence bulk actions.
    - Use 'Reanalyze current project' for full analysis after a quick scan.
ui.source.p0.v.p1.snelstart.1.kies.een.h:
{p0} v{p1}

Quick Start:
1. Choose a root folder, for example D:\Android or D:\scripts.
2. Choose the Normal or Deep scan profile.
3. Click Scan.
4. In Dashboard, click Python, Android, Arduino, etc. to filter immediately.
5. The left panel is scrollable; use the mouse wheel when lower buttons are outside the visible area.
6. Select a project and use the page selector on the right for Details, Release, Documentation, Tools or Output.
7. Use Maintenance > Cleanup dry run before deleting anything.

Safety:
- Cleanup never runs automatically.
- Deletion always requires confirmation.
- Backup before cleanup is enabled by default.

behavioral.v115.case_analysis_title: Case description → evidence extraction → analyst review
behavioral.v115.detected_evidence_hint: CAMT extracts candidate behavioral evidence from the case text. Review, correct or remove items before actor matching.
behavioral.v115.extraction_not_run: Evidence extraction has not been run yet.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_general: Describe what happened in ordinary language. Include only facts that are known; unknown details may be omitted.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_ot_ics: Describe the OT/ICS incident: sector, access path, affected systems, observed protocols, IT→OT movement, tools/malware and explicitly absent behavior where known.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_network: Describe the intrusion path, remote access, lateral movement, affected systems, protocols, tools and any concrete techniques or indicators.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_initial: Describe how access appears to have been obtained: exposed service/appliance, exploit, phishing, credentials, target system and follow-on activity.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_malware: Describe observed malware/tooling behavior, execution, persistence, protocols, affected assets and any known ATT&CK techniques.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_campaign: Paste or describe campaign/case information, including sectors, targets, techniques, tooling, malware, infrastructure behavior and campaign indicators.
behavioral.v115.case_hint_blank: Paste any case narrative or technical notes. CAMT will extract only evidence it can recognize deterministically.
behavioral.v115.case_example_general: An organisation in the energy sector observed exploitation of a public-facing VPN appliance. Valid credentials were then used for remote access and RDP connections to internal Windows systems. PowerShell activity was observed. No destructive activity was identified.
behavioral.v115.case_example_ot_ics: An energy-sector organisation detected exploitation of an internet-facing VPN appliance. After access, valid accounts were used to reach a jump host and later an engineering workstation in the OT environment. RDP and Modbus/TCP traffic were observed. PowerShell was used on Windows systems. No destructive activity or PLC logic modification was observed.
behavioral.v115.case_example_network: An external remote service was used to enter the network. The activity moved from a VPN gateway to a Windows file server using RDP and SMB. PowerShell and PsExec were observed during lateral movement. The affected organisation operates in the energy sector.
behavioral.v115.case_example_initial: A public-facing edge appliance was exploited shortly before an unusual remote session was created. The attacker then used valid accounts over HTTPS and RDP to access internal Windows systems. No phishing activity was observed.
behavioral.v115.case_example_malware: A Windows server executed an unknown payload followed by PowerShell and PsExec activity. HTTPS was used for outbound communications and SMB for movement to another host. The payload established persistence; no destructive behavior was observed.
behavioral.v115.case_example_campaign: Multiple energy-sector organisations reported exploitation of exposed remote-access appliances followed by valid-account use, RDP access and movement toward engineering workstations. Similar PowerShell activity and HTTPS infrastructure were seen across incidents.
